date:

upsc_summary: Double Deflation Methodology: Manufacturing GVA at constant prices is compiled by deflating output and intermediate consumption separately, which can yield negative implicit deflators when input prices rise faster than output prices.
Base Year Revision: National accounts estimates updated to 2022-23 base year, incorporating modern indices such as Producer Price Index (PPI) and Banking Services Price Index (BkSPI).

GDP Deflator vs. CPI & WPI: The implicit GDP deflator measures net value-added prices across the entire economy (including services and government consumption), whereas CPI measures final consumer baskets and WPI measures wholesale commodities.
PFCE Methodology: Double deflation does not apply to Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) as it represents final demand without intermediate consumption.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                02 SEP 2026 8:49PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: Double Deflation Method: Preferred by the IMF for volume GDP estimation; deflates industry gross output and intermediate inputs independently to calculate real GVA.

Implicit GVA Deflator Mechanics: Clarifies that a negative implicit deflator in manufacturing (e.g., -1.5% in Q1 2026-27) results from input inflation outpacing output inflation, not from falling final output prices.
Comparison of Price Indices: Outlines structural reasons for divergence between Implicit GDP Deflator, Consumer Price Index (CPI), and Wholesale Price Index (WPI).
Methodological Updating: Details the benchmark-indicator approach and successive revisions associated with updating national accounting base years to 2022-23.

date:

upsc_summary: Districts as Export Hubs (DEH): Strategic expansion of One District One Product (ODOP) converting districts into core export planning units under the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).
